options.text: The smallest part of the system that runs independently
The largest module in the system

questions.explanation: An architectural quantum is the smallest part that runs independently, with independent deployment, high functional cohesion, and low external coupling.

questions.prompt: Which of these are monolithic architectural styles?
questions.explanation: Monolithic styles: layered, modular monolith, pipeline, and microkernel. Microservices is a distributed style.

questions.prompt: What is the 'sinkhole' anti-pattern risk in layered architecture?

options.text: Requests pass through layers doing nothing but forwarding (no real logic)

questions.explanation: The sinkhole anti-pattern occurs when requests merely pass through layers without processing; ~20% is manageable, ~80% means changing the style.

questions.prompt: What is the trade-off of using 'open' layers (allowing requests to skip layers)?

options.text: More flexibility and performance, but higher coupling risk
More stability and modularity, but slower performance

questions.explanation: Open layers give flexibility and performance but higher coupling risk; closed layers give stability, modularity, and easier changes.

questions.prompt: A modular monolith is domain-partitioned, with each module encapsulating a business capability, yet deployed as a single unit.
questions.explanation: Modular monolith: domain-partitioned modules with strong internal boundaries, deployed as one unit (WAR/EAR/assembly), possibly with dedicated repositories.

questions.prompt: In pipeline (pipes and filters) architecture, filters are ideally...
questions.explanation: Filters are independent and ideally stateless; pipes connect them unidirectionally. Examples: Bash, Zsh, MapReduce.

questions.prompt: Which are filter types in a pipeline architecture?
questions.explanation: Pipeline filter roles: producer, transformer (map), tester (reduce), and consumer (persistence/termination).

options.text: A stable core system extended by plug-in components
Many independent microservices with separate databases
A single layer with no extension points

questions.explanation: Microkernel = a core system with stable 'happy path' functionality extended by plug-ins; plug-ins communicate p2p with the core, not each other. Examples: browsers, IDEs, Jira.

questions.prompt: Among monolithic styles, the layered architecture is rated very high on simplicity but very low on modularity.
questions.explanation: Layered architecture has very high simplicity but very low modularity, maintainability, deployability, and evolvability.
